newsitem.title: USA: U.S. domestic crudes firm late on demand, stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. domestic crudes firm late on demand, stocks.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes firmed late Thursday fuelled by refiner demand for light crudes and drawdowns in crude and heating oil, traders said.
Louisiana light and heavy grades chalked up impressive gains over the moderately busy session, keeping pace with the rise in European crude premiums and diminished imports.
November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $25.35-45 a barrel, up about 30 cents from Wednesday's cash market, with the prompt Nov/Dec spread hovering between 35-40 cents.
Domestic trade focused on Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire differentials, which overtook Light Louisiana Sweet/St James.
"It's not common that HLS makes it to parity against LLS, but we have some locational demand," an East Coast trader said, citing thin availability of light crudes.
Contrary to earlier opinions, refiners who purchased some Brent and Cusiana were not backing out as much supply.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire rallied to 69 cents a barrel over WTI/Cushing, up from the morning's 60 cents premium.
LLS/St James regained some of its recent luster to trade at 62 and 65 cents, compared with 58 cents yesterday.
WTI/Midland, however, drifted lower trading at parity to WTI, down seven cents from Wednesday's high.
For the most part, traders said a narrow arbitrage and high delivered prices for sweet grades amid a drop in overall crude stocks, would continue to lend support.
The Energy Information Administration report Thursday showed crude stocks down 3.3 million barrels compared with the American Petroleum Institute's 417,000 barrels.
Sour grades, meanwhile, were thinly talked facing a little more pressure from regional supplies and more competitive pricing for Oriente crude by Petroecuador.
West Texas Sour/Midland eased to minus $1.42 a barrel, down four cents from Wednesday.
